description: Expert visual-storytelling and authoring bundle for AI agents. Thirteen skills across five authoring areas plus install composition and runtime setup: Flint chart and ThemeSpec language, Print figures, Replicate, Shell, Banner, install-visual-companions, and setup-illustrator-runtime. Shared framing, bounded creative exploration, and verification apply across the authoring areas. Composes with the public Alex_ACT_Core runtime.

authors.name: Microsoft Corporation
authors.role: flint-chart authoring skill body (forked from microsoft/flint-chart/agent-skills/flint-chart-author) + flint-chart-mcp npm package

frontmatter.description: Distill the one-sentence Big Idea, story arc, audience, and style stance for a chart BEFORE picking a chart type. Starts by questioning intent — whether the artifact should exist at all, and whether the stated purpose is the real one. Reads the surrounding docs / prose / ticket for an existing Big Idea first, then helps the user articulate one via a 3-question elicitation ladder if none is found. Asks whether the user wants a TRADITIONAL (safe) or INNOVATIVE (higher-impact, higher-risk) treatment. Use before invoking the flint-chart skill or the /render-chart prompt whenever the user's ask is 'chart this', 'visualize', 'make a chart', 'show the data', or when framing is unclear.

skills.name: chart-vocabulary
skills.role: chart selection + evaluation reference (7-goal catalog, CSAR loop, override decision table, 5-visual rule, gallery pointers, selection decision tree). Deeper reference behind flint-chart §0.2; also invoked when reviewing an AI-suggested chart, sanity-checking dashboard density, or teaching chart taxonomy. Adapted from Alex_ACT_Visual_Storytelling v1.2.0 on 2026-07-30.

frontmatter.description: Reference catalog of chart types organized by seven communication goals (comparison, change-over-time, proportion, distribution, relationship, flow, deviation), plus a CSAR evaluation loop for AI-generated chart choices, override decision table, 5-visual rule for dashboard density, living gallery pointers (FT Visual Vocabulary, Data-to-Viz, Data Viz Catalog, Vega-Lite examples, Storytelling with Data), and a 6-step selection algorithm. Use when picking a chart type, evaluating an AI-suggested chart, reviewing chart choices for story-intent alignment, sanity-checking a dashboard's density, or explaining chart taxonomy to a heir.

Use when the user wants to visualize data — from 'which chart should I use?' to 'render this'. Helps pick the right chart from the analytical question (comparison / trend / distribution / relationship / proportion / flow / KPI), then authors a ChartAssemblyInput and renders via the flint-chart-mcp server (Vega-Lite / ECharts / Chart.js). Transform data before Flint; style tweaks after Flint.

skills.name: flint-theme
skills.role: custom ThemeSpec composition: routes grammar to Flint's version-matched MCP resource, then owns untrusted-reference handling, Theme Lab corpus iteration, and render-verify handoff

frontmatter.description: Creates and refines reusable Flint ThemeSpec visual systems from brand guidance, websites, decks, design tokens, or publication references. Use when a user asks for a custom Flint theme, wants to translate a visual identity into charts, or needs to test theme behavior across a chart corpus.

skills.name: render-verify
skills.role: verification (runs after rendering; closes the loop the flint-chart skill deliberately opens). Not chart-specific — applies to any rendered visual artifact

frontmatter.description: Verify a rendered visual artifact actually says what it was supposed to say — open it, read its console errors, walk a failure catalog, and check it against the claim it was meant to carry. Works on charts, generated HTML reports, SVG, dashboards, diagrams, and any other output meant to be looked at. Use after render_chart / create_chart_view, after editing a post-Flint Vega-Lite spec, and before committing any generated HTML/SVG/PNG. Satisfied by the host's built-in browser tools or by the optional playwright MCP server.

skills.name: corpus-qa-sweep
skills.role: corpus-scale verification (sweeps every item against machine-checkable invariants, then triages each flag). Pairs with render-verify: this one finds candidates across the corpus, render-verify judges one. Extracted 2026-08-06 from a 67-document sweep in which 4 of 6 first-pass findings were harness defects rather than product defects.

frontmatter.description: Run a QA sweep across an entire corpus instead of one sample: instrument the real output boundary, assert machine-checkable invariants, sweep every item, then triage every flag before believing it. Works on doc sites, generated pages, chart batches, report sets, prose, and formatting. Use when a change to a renderer, template, generator, or shared component affects many outputs, when someone asks to check all the pages or wants no surprises before a release, or when a single-sample pass feels like thin evidence. For judging one rendered artifact against a failure catalog, use render-verify instead.

skills.name: docs-shell
skills.role: documentation viewer / gallery renderer — the single-page HTML shell (index.html + manifest.json at one stable shell root) that renders concatenated markdown as browsable docs with two-line topnav, per-doc emoji icons, sticky page header, and sidebar TOC. Not chart-specific; serves as a natural preview surface for any authored visual (chart galleries, illustration catalogs, generated report indices). Ported from Alex_ACT_Steward on 2026-07-29; this plugin is now the canonical source-of-truth.

frontmatter.description: The single-page HTML shell (index.html + manifest.json at a repository root or stable subfolder) that renders concatenated markdown as browsable, GitHub-styled documentation with a two-line topnav, per-doc emoji icons, sticky page header, and sidebar TOC. Ships the canvas + typography grammar (viewBoxes, print-legibility floor with math, type hierarchy, font stack, data-print-role markers, text-fits ladder), a Tailwind-grounded semantic palette (Blue = correct, Red = critique, Green = approval, Amber triple-duty, Grays scaffolding), and four structural composition idioms (BEFORE/AFTER paired panels with badges, numbered critique callouts, family-band abstracts, 5-Visual Rule dashboards). Use when authoring SVG figures for print, when reviewing a figure for print legibility, or when picking colors for a figure whose colors will carry meaning across a book or report.

skills.name: figure-generator
skills.role: deterministic hand-authored SVG generator discipline (.mjs pattern reading from data/<slug>.json, data-sha256 audit hash embed, dataset-first rule + contract tests, dataset inversion from approved sample SVG, fix-in-generator-never-in-SVG rule, figure-count hoist)

frontmatter.description: Ship deterministic hand-authored SVG generators for print-quality figures backed by real published datasets. Ships the .mjs generator pattern reading from data/<slug>.json, the data-sha256 audit hash embed for provenance, the dataset-first rule with contract tests pinning headline numbers, the dataset-inversion procedure for reverse-engineering data from an approved sample SVG, the fix-in-generator-never-in-SVG rule, and the figure-count hoist to one JSON. Use when authoring reproducible book or report figures, when a figure's numbers might drift silently, or when reverse-engineering data from a graphic whose dataset is missing.

skills.role: thin routing + brand alignment for AI image generation and editing on Replicate; delegates substantive prompting to Replicate's upstream prompt-images / find-models / run-models / compare-models skills (npx skills add replicate/skills)

prompts.name: setup-illustrator-runtime
prompts.role: namespaced preview-and-provision entry point for offline MCP runtime readiness

frontmatter.description: Audit Illustrator's stable MCP versions, preview and install exact reviewed pins through npm's configured registry, then verify direct Node launches. Use when checking for updates, after installing or updating Illustrator, or when private runtime state is missing.

mcp.merge: additive — merge each server entry into any existing server map; overwriting the file destroys the user's other servers
mcp.path_notes: VS Code does NOT read a workspace-root .mcp.json — that is the Claude Code convention. Same 'servers' schema, different path, and VS Code reports no error because it reads no file at all. GitHub Copilot CLI differs twice over: different path AND a different top-level key ('mcpServers', not 'servers'), so a pasted 'servers' block fails just as silently; prefer its '/mcp add' command.

servers.notes: Exact 0.5.0 package installed once through the configured npm registry into a plugin-private runtime. The direct Node launcher starts no npm or npx process. Adds ThemeSpec discovery plus version-matched chart and theme authoring resources. Version changes require an explicit compatibility review.

servers.role: connects the agent to Replicate's HTTP API for AI image / video generation, model discovery, comparison, and prediction execution
servers.optional_because: Only needed when the replicate-imagery skill fires. Users who never generate AI imagery pay no cost and see no failure; the MCP server starts on demand and fails auth only if invoked without REPLICATE_API_TOKEN set.
servers.prereq: REPLICATE_API_TOKEN environment variable. Get one at https://replicate.com/account/api-tokens. Set in shell env; the plugin's mcp.json references `${env:REPLICATE_API_TOKEN}` so the token never enters source control.
servers.notes: Exact 0.9.0 package installed once through the configured npm registry into a plugin-private runtime. The direct Node launcher starts no npm or npx process. Covers models.search, models.list, models.get, predictions.create, predictions.get, and the rest of the HTTP API surface.

servers.role: satisfies the render-verify skill's browser capability on hosts without built-in browser tools — primarily GitHub Copilot CLI, which is a terminal agent and has none
servers.optional_because: VS Code Copilot heirs already have built-in browser/screenshot tools that open file:// with no flags and no browser download — measured 2026-07-25 against demos/heart-with-axes/report.html. Omit this entry on VS Code; the render-verify skill names the capability, not the product.
servers.version_pin: exact — caret on 0.0.x expands to >=0.0.78 <0.0.79 and protects nothing while reading as if it does. Note the MCP handshake reports the underlying Playwright library version (e.g. 1.62.0-alpha-…), NOT the package version; do not pin against it.

flags.--headless: verification pass, not a demo — no visible window
flags.--isolated: no persistent browser profile; keeps the user's real session out of it
flags.--browser msedge: chosen for the heir population, which is predominantly corpnet Windows where Edge ships with the OS and Chrome is frequently absent. The upstream default is an installed Google Chrome, which fails on exactly those machines. Override with --browser chrome|firefox|webkit where Edge is not present (most Linux).
flags.--allow-unrestricted-file-access: REQUIRED for file:// navigation, which is blocked outright by default. Security trade-off: the browser can then read any file the user can. Acceptable for verifying local artifacts; do NOT combine this server with untrusted web browsing.

servers.notes: No bundled browser — Playwright drives an INSTALLED browser by channel. Machines without the selected channel fail loudly ('Browser distribution ... is not found'); switch channel or run 'npx playwright install <channel>'. The server writes .playwright-mcp/ artifacts into the launch cwd — gitignore it, and never pass a bare filename to browser_take_screenshot or it lands in the repo root instead.

settings.role: registers the local/ skill + prompt discovery roots
settings.merge: additive — merge these two keys into any existing settings.json; never disable VS Code's default roots, since an adopter's own skills and prompts live there
settings.notes: VS Code discovers skills in .github/skills/ and prompts in .github/prompts/ but does not search their subfolders, so this plugin's local/ install paths load nothing without these keys — silently, with no error, the same failure mode as the .mcp.json path trap. Alex ACT Edition heirs >=3.x already register these roots and can skip this asset.

flint: /render-chart prompt fires — OR the user asks for a chart ambiently and flint-chart loads directly
load chart-big-idea skill → earn-a-figure gate → explanatory/exploratory/persuasive intent → Big Idea → arc → audience → style + theme/tone stance → Brief
inspect actual rows, units, cardinality, totals, outliers, and context; transform upstream when the analytical question requires it
author one data + semantic_types truth layer; enrich ambiguous fields with intrinsicDomain, unit, or sortOrder
load chart-vocabulary technique router + flint-chart; for open-ended work author one familiar and one expressive treatment that differ materially in chart_spec, arrangement, technique, or theme
call list_themes for a preset OR load flint-theme → flint://theme-skill / author_flint_theme → Theme Lab corpus iteration
render serious candidates via flint MCP (create_chart_view | render_chart); use validate_chart and compile_chart for their narrower contracts
load render-verify → inspect errors + failure catalog + first focal point + reading order + context + accessibility + Big Idea visibility
iterate the smallest responsible layer → report selected treatment, verification evidence, caption/alt text, and strongest rejected alternative
fast path: diagnostic chart, fully formed spec, or explicit treatment skips alternative generation
print_figures: user asks for a book / report figure OR the print-svg-style-guide skill loads ambiently
load chart-big-idea skill → Step 0.5 earn-a-figure gate (does the artifact belong on paper?) → emit Brief
load print-svg-style-guide skill → pick composition idiom (BEFORE/AFTER paired panels | numbered critique callouts | family-band abstract | 5-Visual Rule dashboard) + Tailwind semantic palette
load figure-generator skill → author data/<slug>.json + contract test → write .mjs generator with print-legibility floor math + data-sha256 audit hash → emit SVG to assets/figures/
load render-verify skill → SVG XML validity + Prose-coupling check
replicate: user asks for an illustration / hero image / AI-generated image
load chart-big-idea skill → Step 0.5 (does the artifact earn AI generation, or would a chart / diagram / prose serve better?)
load replicate-imagery skill → pick model family (FLUX / Ideogram / Recraft / Imagen) + cost tier + brand alignment via brand-palette hex codes
upstream replicate/skills bundle composes the prompt (installed via `npx skills add replicate/skills`)
replicate MCP server calls predictions.create on the Replicate HTTP API (requires REPLICATE_API_TOKEN)
load render-verify skill → Prose-coupling check catches AI hallucinations against the intended message
shell: user asks to set up a browsable / gallery / catalog surface
load docs-shell skill → copy the complete starter/ bundle to workspace root or configured docs folder
author markdown source files; shell renders concatenated markdown as a single-page HTML shell with two-line topnav, sticky page header, sidebar TOC
HTML-source docs (pre-built Flint reports, exported dashboards) bypass the shell wrapper

prerequisites.mcp_host: VS Code Copilot 1.118+ | Claude Desktop | Cursor | GitHub Copilot CLI | any MCP stdio client
prerequisites.browser: Only if using the optional 'playwright' server: an installed Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or WebKit. No browser ships with the package. Not needed on hosts with built-in browser tools (e.g. VS Code Copilot).
prerequisites.alex_host: Alex_ACT_Steward brain (primary, plugin-native lineage) OR Alex_ACT_Edition >=3.x heir (v4.1.0 compatibility line) with local/ skill+prompt roots registered
prerequisites.vscode_settings: On a plain VS Code workspace (no Alex ACT Steward brain or Edition heir), the assets.settings keys must be present or the local/ install paths are never discovered.
prerequisites.replicate_api_token: Optional — only required if using the replicate-imagery skill. Get one at https://replicate.com/account/api-tokens and set REPLICATE_API_TOKEN in your shell environment. The plugin's mcp.json references ${env:REPLICATE_API_TOKEN} so the token stays out of source control.
prerequisites.runtime_provisioning: Run setup-illustrator-runtime --check-updates to audit stable dist-tags, then run setup once after install or update. It uses npm's configured registry and exact reviewed versions; MCP startup uses the direct private launcher.
